gap: No result ChatGPT got states how Husqvarna's AWD Automower actually did in rain over a season: Trusted Reviews ran the 435X AWD for about four months on roughly 4,000 m² with pond banks up to 45 degrees, and it got stuck twice in that time, once in pouring rain on a bank steeper than 50 degrees. ChatGPT's answers put Husqvarna first on maker claims alone.
standout_why: I compared against MowScout's rain guide, The Verge's group test, MowerBench's two-season roundup, Popular Mechanics' LUBA 3 review, MowReview's AWD list and Robovations' wet-grass comparison. MowerBench (cited) already reports the LUBA 3 climbing a 20-degree slope in wet grass without slipping, and the X430 clumping more in damp grass. The Verge (cited) already reports LUBA 3 turf damage on damp ground and the X430 never getting stuck. MowScout and MowReview hold no measurements and say no tester ran the Husqvarna AWD in the wet. Neither MowScout nor MowReview, nor any other result, reports a Husqvarna AWD wet-weather test with figures. Each chat's answer says its Husqvarna pick rests on 'a manufacturer capability claim'.
decides: It gives the Husqvarna AWD pick its first hands-on rain evidence: about four months, two stuck events, and wheels cleared roughly every two weeks in autumn on 45-degree-plus banks. The test is from 2020 and used the 435X AWD with a boundary wire, not the current 435 iQ AWD, so the page must name the model it covers. The other two picks keep their known trade-off. The LUBA 3 AWD has the most wet-traction evidence (20-degree wet slope, no slip, from MowerBench; heavy rain, from The Technology Man), but it loses grip and tears damp turf on tight turns (The Verge; The Technology Man). The X430 does better on damp turf but clumps more (MowerBench). No named lab result for wet cut quality is public, so the findings back no single winner on cut quality.

findings.label: Steepest bank handled in the dry
findings.value: 45 degrees (about 100%), against a 70% (35 degree) design rating
findings.source_title: Husqvarna Automower 435X AWD review | Trusted Reviews
findings.note: Trusted Reviews, published 2020-05-04, reviewer not named on the page. Test field of about 4,000 m² (main lawn about 120 m x 50 m, with a 40 m pond whose banks reach 45 degrees). The reviewer says it 'didn't so much as waver' on that slope in the dry. Read through r.jina.ai because the page returned HTTP 530.

findings.label: Stuck events over about four months, rain included
findings.value: 2 in about four months; one was in pouring rain, nose-down in a soil crack on a bank over 50 degrees
findings.source_title: Husqvarna Automower 435X AWD review | Trusted Reviews
findings.note: One summer season of mowing. The other stuck event was a plastic case jammed on a tree root. In autumn the reviewer had to clear the wheels about once every couple of weeks to keep traction on the steepest banks. The deck and wheels 'resisted clogging', and the review calls the mower 'Unstoppable come rain or shine'. This is the 2020 wired 435X AWD, not the current 435 iQ AWD.

Mammotion told The Verge that sharp turning from a turning-logic update can tear grass and that later software updates followed. Read through r.jina.ai.

findings.label: Labs that score damp-grass cutting
findings.value: Which? runs a 4-week grass-cutting test that includes wet grass; per-model results are for members only
